public.regime_lens: 🚦 RED — SHOCK ESCALATING, METALS RESILIENT (mechanical derivation; operator card holds YELLOW, see §1.3): the axis of stress rotated this week, so the read is RED but for the opposite reason it was RED last week — the two silver-side RED-DEEPENS triggers that fired last week both un-fired, with silver bouncing +5.5% WoW to reclaim $58 (weekly close $58.74, widening the $52 hard-stop buffer back to ~$6.7 from ~$3.70) and gold recovering above $4,000 (~$4,052) to pull G:S back to ~69 and clear the 72 regime-shift line, yet the base regime stays RED because the geopolitical shock and the macro rails escalated hard in their place; a Bab al-Mandeb second front opened as the Houthis attacked two Saudi tankers and declared an embargo on Riyadh, and that second front is one of the operator's own written RED-CASCADE triggers, which fired on its face even though the confirming price action did not follow (oil under the $105 gate, credit benign, metals up), so it is escalated as the #1 sign-off ambiguity rather than acted on; Brent broke $100 intraday for the first time since May (~+16% WoW, ~+30% month-to-date) but eased to $96-98 and remains ~$5-8 under the gate; TNX broke cleanly higher to 4.679 (intraweek 4.703), no longer oscillating across the 4.55 abort but decisively above it, keeping new-tranche deploys mechanically BLOCKED; USDINR held just above 96 (reduce-25 rail still breached but not extending); and the offsets that made this a deepening-not-a-cascade last week are all still intact but with visibly thinner cushions on every one — DXY 101.47 with only ~0.5 to the 102 gate, CCC OAS 991bp ~9bp from 1,000, India VIX 14.03 with NIFTY now down a fifth straight session, and RBI reserves building a third week to $676.24B; the operative watch has rotated fully from silver-downside to shock-and-rails-upside — the numbers that matter now are Brent $105, DXY 102, CCC 1,000, and the FOMC on 7/28-29 into a live two-front war · base: Geopolitical Stagflation over Policy Transition, hawkish, now re-tightening through both realised levels (TNX broke higher, oil broke $100) and forward oil-inflation expectations rather than through metals alone → TIGHTENING · shock: IRAN/HORMUZ PLUS A NEW BAB AL-MANDEB FRONT — the maritime conflict went two-front: the US reached a 13th straight day of strikes on Iran with talks ruled out on both sides, and the Houthis opened a second theatre by attacking two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and declaring a maritime embargo against Riyadh, forcing three Saudi crude tankers to reverse course around Bab al-Mandeb;
